tasks.title: HTTP client retry with exponential backoff and jitter

taskSpec.requirements:
Add resilient retries to the HTTP client in this repository.
- Route requests through a retry loop in src/http.ts while preserving the existing request(url, options) API.
- Implement exponential backoff with full jitter in src/retry.ts. For retry number n (1-based), the delay must be a random value in [0, min(maxDelayMs, baseDelayMs * 2^(n-1))].
- Retry network failures, HTTP 429, and HTTP 5xx. Do not retry other 4xx responses.
- Honor a Retry-After header for 429/503 when present, but never sleep longer than maxDelayMs.
- Honor maxAttempts: the total number of attempts must never exceed it.
- Keep per-attempt timeouts working; explain how timeoutMs interacts with retries.
- Add tests for first-attempt success, retry then success, retry exhaustion, non-retryable 4xx, and delay bounds/jitter.

steps.title: Add full-jitter exponential backoff helpers to retry.ts
steps.verification: Implement computeBackoffDelay(policy, attemptNumber) returning Math.random() * Math.min(policy.maxDelayMs, policy.baseDelayMs * 2 ** (attemptNumber - 1)) for 1-based attempt numbers, a parseRetryAfter(headerValue) helper that parses seconds or HTTP-date into ms (returning undefined when absent/invalid), and a waitForRetry(policy, attemptNumber, retryAfterMs) helper that delays min(retryAfterMs ?? computedJitter, policy.maxDelayMs) using the existing sleep(). Keep RetryPolicy and sleep exported unchanged. Verify with npx tsc --noEmit and add unit tests in tests/retry.test.ts asserting delays are within [0, min(maxDelayMs, baseDelayMs*2^(n-1))], never exceed maxDelayMs, Retry-After is honored, Retry-After above maxDelayMs is clamped, and repeated draws produce varied values (jitter).

steps.title: Route request() through a bounded retry loop with per-attempt timeout
steps.verification: In src/http.ts keep the request(url, options) signature and add an optional retry policy (e.g. options.retry or a module-level default from src/config.ts). Wrap the fetch in a loop up to maxAttempts; use AbortController so each attempt's timeoutMs aborts only that attempt (timeout aborts count as retryable network failures; the full request may take up to maxAttempts * timeoutMs plus backoff sleeps). Retry on thrown/network errors, 429, and 5xx; return the response for 2xx; throw immediately on non-retryable 4xx. On 429/503 read Retry-After and pass it through waitForRetry so sleeps never exceed maxDelayMs. Verify with npx tsc --noEmit and npx jest tests/http.test.ts.

steps.title: Add HTTP retry tests covering all required scenarios
steps.verification: Add tests mocking global fetch with jest.fn and using fake timers to assert: (1) first-attempt success calls fetch exactly once; (2) 503 then 200 succeeds with two calls and a backoff sleep in bounds; (3) persistent 5xx throws after exactly maxAttempts calls with no extra sleep after the last attempt; (4) 400/404 throws after one call with no retry; (5) 429 with Retry-After waits the header value (clamped to maxDelayMs); (6) timeoutMs aborts a slow attempt via AbortController and the next attempt is made. Run npx jest tests/http.test.ts tests/retry.test.ts and npx tsc --noEmit.

steps.title: Wire defaults and exports
steps.verification: Expose default retry policy values (maxAttempts, baseDelayMs, maxDelayMs, default timeoutMs) in src/config.ts, import them in src/http.ts as the default when no policy is supplied, and re-export the retry helpers/types from src/index.ts without breaking existing exports. Verify with npx tsc --noEmit and the full suite npx jest.

risks: Per-attempt timeoutMs means total wall-clock time can reach maxAttempts * timeoutMs plus backoff; callers expecting a single timeoutMs bound may be surprised, so document this clearly.
Using real setTimeout in tests can be slow/flaky; fake timers must be advanced in lockstep with the retry loop or tests will hang.
Math.random-based jitter makes exact delay assertions impossible; tests must assert bounds/ranges rather than exact values.
Parsing Retry-After as an HTTP-date is locale/timezone sensitive and should fall back to computed backoff when invalid.
If fetch throws synchronously or the abort fires after resolution, double-settlement or unhandled rejections can occur unless AbortController is cleaned up per attempt.

tasks.title: Cursor pagination and limit validation for the list API

taskSpec.requirements:
Add cursor-based pagination and limit validation to the list API.
- Extend ListRequest in src/types.ts with an optional cursor and limit.
- In src/api/list.ts, listItems must return a stable page ordered by item id plus nextPage: string | null.
- limit must be an integer from 1 to 100 inclusive, defaulting to 50. Reject invalid limits (0, negative, >100, non-integer, non-number) with ApiError status 400 from src/api/errors.ts.
- The cursor must be opaque. Decode it defensively; a malformed cursor must produce ApiError status 400, never a 500.
- nextPage must be null on the last page, otherwise a cursor that round-trips to the next item.
- Add tests for the first page, second page, last page, invalid limits, and malformed cursors.

tasks.title: Fix auth token refresh: dedupe concurrent refreshes and handle expiry

taskSpec.requirements:
Fix token refresh in the authentication module.
- getAccessToken() in src/auth.ts currently refreshes separately for every concurrent caller.
- Deduplicate concurrent refreshes: while a refresh is in flight, all callers must await the same promise and receive the same new token.
- Treat a token as expired when Date.now() >= expiresAt - skewMs with skewMs = 30_000, so a token that will expire during the request is refreshed first.
- On refresh success, update the cached token and resolve every waiter. On failure, reject every waiter with the same error, clear the in-flight promise, and allow a later call to retry.
- Never deadlock: clear the in-flight state in a finally block.
- Preserve the public getAccessToken() signature and the existing test setup.
- Add or update tests in src/auth.test.ts for: 10 concurrent callers cause exactly one store.refresh call; an expired token refreshes; a token inside the 30-second skew refreshes; a fresh token does not refresh; a failed refresh clears state and a later attempt succeeds.

tasks.title: Structured JSON logging with request IDs

taskSpec.requirements:
Add structured JSON logging and request IDs to the server.
- Rewrite src/logger.ts so every record is one line of JSON with at least timestamp (ISO 8601), level, message, requestId, and any extra fields merged in. Do not use string concatenation for the record.
- Support debug/info/warn/error levels with a threshold from LOG_LEVEL (default info). Make the output sink injectable for tests; default to stdout.
- In src/request-context.ts, store the current request ID in AsyncLocalStorage. Use the incoming x-request-id header when present, otherwise generate one with crypto.randomUUID().
- In src/server.ts, run each request inside the request context, include the request ID in every log record, return it as the x-request-id response header, and include requestId in error response bodies.
- Add tests in tests/logger.test.ts and tests/server.test.ts for JSON shape / one line per record, level filtering, request ID propagation, honoring an incoming x-request-id, and returning a generated request ID.
